blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 11 sold over 4 months against an average of 23.5 listed, about 8.5 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was August with 5 sold. Condos and townhomes: 0 sold over 4 months against an average of 3.8 listed.

faq.a: Burnaby's eastern quadrant — the residential east side between the Edmonds town centre and the New Westminster border, taking in Robert Burnaby Park, Cariboo Hill and the Second Street and Twelfth Avenue neighbourhoods; it is a GVR MLS® sub-area name, not one small neighbourhood.

faq.q: Which schools are on Burnaby's east side?
faq.a: SD41 schools on the Province's list include Second Street Community Elementary (K–7), 7502 2nd St, Twelfth Avenue Elementary (K–7), 7622 12th Ave, Taylor Park Elementary (K–7), 7590 Mission Ave, and Cariboo Hill Secondary (8–12), 8580 16th Ave; catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.

The east side's large forested park — the City describes many creeks and streams running through it and over half its area as critical wildlife habitat, and is restoring it with invasive-species removal and 3,000 new trees; its courts are listed at 3 tennis and 10 pickleball.

faq.q: How is transit on the east side?
faq.a: Edmonds Station on the Expo Line serves the west side of the area, and route 116 links Edmonds Station to Metrotown Station through south and east Burnaby via Griffiths Drive, Southridge Drive, 18th Avenue and Marine Way.
